Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 15:32 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Sana Patel (Marigold, Head of ML Ops), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng Manager), Liam O'Connor (Security Arch), Priyanka Rao (Product Owner)

Auto Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on Marigold's activation, decide initial deployment mode, confirm security requirements and pilot success criteria — see action items.

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Avery Collins: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving out time. We're going to run through a quick agenda — introductions, goals for the pilot, security overview, deployment options, then finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:08] Sana Patel: Yeah that works. Quick context from our side — we're partway through standardizing LLM features across a few products, want a predictable inference tier. Key concerns are data residency and auditability, plus keeping latency under 200ms p50 for our chat flow.
[00:23] Ethan Cole: And we also need to understand network model: will Redwood sit in our VPC or are we doing a hosted integration? We have existing Egress restrictions, so that matters.
[00:33] Avery Collins: Totally. High level, we offer three modes — hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private deployment for VPC / on-prem. Diego can walk through the tradeoffs.
[00:42] Diego Ruiz: Yeah, quick note — dedicated gives you predictable QPS with reserved GPU pools, private puts a control plane in your VPC and you manage keys, etc. Tradeoffs are mostly around operational burden and cost. For the latency target you mentioned, dedicated or private are both viable; hosted can hit low latency too depending on region and model choice.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Sorry to interrupt — our security team will insist on customer-managed KMS for key rotation, and we need full audit logs. Does Redwood support HSM/KMS integrations?
[01:13] Avery Collins: We do — Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted we provide encryption at rest and in transit; for dedicated you can bring a managed KMS through our enterprise plan. We'll attach the security pack with specifics.
[01:29] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with the SOC 2 artifacts and the template for the network security questionnaire.
[01:36] Priyanka Rao: Timeline wise we're aiming for a pilot in Q3, ideally two weeks of smoke tests then a small production ramp. Success criteria: under 200ms p50, less than 5% error rate, and throughput of 50 qps sustained.
[01:51] Diego Ruiz: Helpful numbers. For 50 qps and typical 1k-token prompts we'll want to size batch windows and see if KV caching helps. When you say 1k tokens, is that average or peak?
[02:05] Sana Patel: Average is about 600-900 tokens, peaks up to 1.2k for long form. The chat flow mixes short and long so latency sensitivity varies.
[02:15] Diego Ruiz: Understood. We'll propose batching and quantization settings. Also want to flag that prefix caching (we sometimes call it KV cache) can reduce repeated prefix costs, but it depends on prompt variability.
[02:29] Ethan Cole: About the model: we're evaluating open models and may want to bring models from our internal registry. Does Redwood support bringing custom model artifacts?
[02:38] Avery Collins: Yes — Redwood can serve customer-provided model files in Private, and we have a model onboarding flow for dedicated as well. There are compatibility checks (tokenizer, architecture) but Diego can scope that.
[02:48] Diego Ruiz: On compatibility, the key is checkpoint format and whether we've got kernels optimized for the architecture. We'll run a quick onboarding test with a small model to validate runtime.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: Regarding network: we have strict egress controls, so if you need to reach back to a control plane, it must be over a pinned IP or via a peering connection. Is that supported?
[03:08] Avery Collins: For Private we can operate with a customer-controlled control plane that doesn't require broad egress — peering or dedicated express route works. We'll include network diagrams.
[03:18] Priyanka Rao: Can you walk through the pilot scope again? What specifically will Redwood benchmark?
[03:25] Diego Ruiz: Pilot plan in high level: 1) Baseline functional smoke test with a canned prompt set, 2) Throughput and latency benchmarks across sample datasets, 3) Failure mode tests (node drain, region failover), and 4) Monitoring and cost capture. We'll need a sample of representative prompts and a preferred metric sheet from you.
[03:47] Sana Patel: I'll try to provide a 20k prompt sample set, scrubbed, and a couple of typical conversation traces. We need to check with legal on sharing though — names and PII redaction.
[03:58] Maya Chen: Totally expect that; we can accept synthetic or anonymized data. We'll note that in the sample request.
[04:04] Ethan Cole: One thing — our infra team prefers Terraform examples for any VPC peering and route setup. Do you have IaC templates?
[04:12] Diego Ruiz: We have Terraform and CloudFormation snippets for VPC peering, security groups, and route tables — will attach. Some of them are auto-generated for the Private installer as well.
[04:21] Sana Patel: On compliance, besides SOC 2, we may have to show evidence of SSO and RBAC granularity for certain user roles. Can we have RBAC scoped to token-level in Redwood Console?
[04:32] Avery Collins: Yes, Redwood Console supports RBAC and token scoping; we can map to your internal SAML groups. We'll include the SSO setup guide.
[04:41] Liam O'Connor: Also need rolling audit logs for two years in case of internal audits. Is long-term log retention an add-on?
[04:48] Maya Chen: Retention is configurable; long-term retention for logs is an add-on or enterprise tier. We'll include pricing for archival.
[04:55] Priyanka Rao: Cost control is important — can Redwood show per-route and per-token breakdowns during the pilot?
[05:02] Avery Collins: Yep, Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns. For the pilot we'll enable detailed traces so you can see per-prompt cost.
[05:09] Diego Ruiz: Quick technical note — quantization will lower memory footprint and cost but may slightly change output quality. We'll flag tradeoffs when we present model recommendations.
[05:20] Ethan Cole: For the initial pilot, is it reasonable to start hosted while we spin up private/dedicated? We want to validate functionality quickly.
[05:28] Avery Collins: That's a pattern we've seen a lot — start with hosted to get functionality verified, then move to dedicated or private for performance and compliance. Might add a brief step for production cutover plan.
[05:36] Sana Patel: I like that. We'll need to know the delta in latency and cost between hosted and dedicated for our workload.
[05:44] Diego Ruiz: We'll run cost modeling based on your sample traces. Could you send the token distribution and typical concurrency?
[05:51] Priyanka Rao: Concurrency target for pilot is 30 concurrent sessions, ramping to 50 qps.
[05:57] Diego Ruiz: Good — that'll help size the initial pool.
[06:03] Avery Collins: Quick check on stakeholders and approvals — who signs off on security and production go?
[06:10] Liam O'Connor: Security sign-off will be me and our Head of InfoSec, Naomi Price. Production owner will be Priyanka and the SRE team; they'll handle runbooks.
[06:20] Maya Chen: We'll prepare a basic runbook template and an escalation matrix to align.
[06:26] Ethan Cole: On observability, how do you export traces and integrate with our existing Datadog setup?
[06:33] Diego Ruiz: We can push metrics and traces to Datadog and also provide webhooks for events. We'll provide an example config.
[06:41] Sana Patel: Are there any hard limits on model size or sequence length we should anticipate for private deployment?
[06:48] Diego Ruiz: Not hard limits per se, but performance profiles change. If you want to serve very large seq lengths frequently, kernel selection and memory layout impact cost. We'll recommend a quantization profile if you need to reduce memory.
[06:59] Priyanka Rao: Okay can we talk about the actual timeline — you said Q3 pilot. What are the Weeks and owners?
[07:06] Avery Collins: Proposed timeline: Week 1 (this week to next) — security docs + sample dataset exchange; Week 2 — infra setup and baseline smoke tests; Week 3 — throughput/latency benchmarks and failure mode tests; Week 4 — results review and go/no-go for ramp.
[07:22] Sana Patel: That aligns with internal urgency. If we can get the security pack by Friday, I'll push legal to expedite.
[07:30] Avery Collins: We'll send it tomorrow. Maya will own the packet.
[07:34] Maya Chen: Copy — I'll send SOC 2, SSO guide, network templates, and the sample request spreadsheet.
[07:41] Diego Ruiz: For the benchmark, if you can provide a 10-20k prompt sample and typical concurrency patterns we'll generate a cost/latency model and a recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[07:54] Ethan Cole: Regarding access controls, can we map roles in Redwood to our internal groups? We want read-only for devs and admin for platform.
[08:01] Avery Collins: Yes, through SAML provisioning we can map groups to Console roles.
[08:06] Priyanka Rao: A question on model lifecycle — once we onboard a model, how are rollouts and versioning handled?
[08:12] Diego Ruiz: We support model versioning and can do canary rollouts with traffic splits, and automatic fallback policies if the new version crosses error thresholds. We'll demo that in the SE deep dive.
[08:24] Sana Patel: For fallback policies, can you do cross-region fallback?
[08:28] Diego Ruiz: Yep — smart routing supports region and tier fallback. We'll show a sample config.
[08:34] Liam O'Connor: One more security point — we need to demonstrate data deletion/retention for compliance. How granular is deletion?
[08:42] Avery Collins: We support token-level retention policies and can expire KV cache and logs on schedules. We'll include that in the security pack.
[08:50] Priyanka Rao: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side to start?
[08:54] Avery Collins: No blockers — main thing is we need your sample data and network contacts. Also to confirm pilot window dates.
[08:59] Ethan Cole: I'll loop in infra and share contact by Monday.
[09:04] Sana Patel: I'll check legal for the sample data and get back by Tuesday.
[09:08] Avery Collins: Perfect. Recap of action items: Redwood sends security pack and Terraform snippets; Diego to send benchmark plan; Marigold to share dataset sample and infra contacts. Set next meeting for technical deep dive — target 2026-07-24. Anything else?
[09:22] Priyanka Rao: Not from me. Thanks everyone.
[09:25] Avery Collins: Thanks — we'll follow up with notes and the security pack tomorrow.

(End of recording)
